html:
SMTO-LLM-0104 — Reading the image was stopped

GUID: 1774c646-350d-58f8-bdc1-30368ab34c24
Slug: vision-stopped
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: vision

What happened

  • SMTO stopped looking at the image because the task was stopped or given new instructions. No description of the image was produced; earlier results in the task are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the Conversation to see whether Stop was selected or new instructions were sent while SMTO was reading the image. Either one ends the image reading on purpose, so nothing else needs fixing.
  2. If you didn't stop the task, select Timeline at the top of the Conversation to show its activity and see why the image reading stopped. A safety rule or time limit can also stop the reading, and the activity timeline shows which one.
  3. If you still want the image read, ask SMTO about it again in the same Conversation. Results SMTO already finished in that task are kept. The stopped attempt produced no description, so a new request is needed.

What success looks like

  • A new request returns a description of the image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat the image as reviewed; this attempt produced no description.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The synchronous Vision observation was cancelled (user stop, superseding instructions, I/O cancellation or a runtime policy stop) before it produced an observation.

What this means

  • The synchronous observation unwound after cancellation or superseding instructions. Its lifecycle receipt, rather than this diagnostic title, establishes completion and slot release. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The synchronous observation unwound after cancellation or superseding instructions. Its lifecycle receipt, rather than this diagnostic title, establishes completion and slot release.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's operation lifecycle receipt for the cancellation cause (user cancel, supersession, I/O cancellation or a RuntimePolicyError stop, which is recorded as failed) and confirm the operation ended and released its activity slot. Request a fresh observation only if it is still wanted; completed task results are retained.
  • Inspect the stopped run’s state. Continue only if the image observation is still wanted; retain already completed task results.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The stopped operation is ended and its resource claim released; a requested continuation can make a fresh bounded observation.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
